review_kind: All remaining Awesome Copilot skill packages (313 exact pinned complete packages), individual 10-dimension static candidate reviews; NOT governed review, security scan or behavioral validation
review_method: Parallel read-only reviewers on disjoint exact package lists with one shared brief; complete package files read at the exact pin; integration owner validated identity, taxonomy, score/rationale agreement and hard-fail/disposition consistency and adjudicated conflicts (reconciliation_overrides). Nothing executed, installed or fetched from candidates.
macro_findings: Every remaining pinned Awesome Copilot skill package (313 direct-shape, 177 single-file and 136 multi-file including scripts, references, templates and assets) was read as a complete package by 19 parallel read-only reviewers; binary assets were recorded by type and a handful of >60 KB generated data files were characterised rather than read line by line (noted per record).

47 packages fail the authority hard gate: pushes, PR creation and thread resolution without per-action confirmation (copilot-pr-autopilot, github-release, make-repo-contribution, workshop-create, repo-standardizer), live cloud/tenant/Store changes (azure-devops-cli with --yes, azure-static-web-apps production deploys, entra-agent-user, msstore-cli, foundry-agent-sync, powerbi-modeling, snowflake-semanticview), DNS changes (namecheap), destructive file operations (document converters that rmtree output folders) and persistent agent-memory writes without approval (audit-integrity).

Privacy: six packages read or send private data without consent (clipboard, colleague email and meetings, calendar/chat pre-fill, production LLM traces to third-party judges, vendor usage telemetry); secret handling defects include printed deploy tokens, plaintext DB passwords echoed back, passwords solicited in chat, API keys in query strings and hard-coded weak passwords.
Ten packages fetch-and-follow remote content or install unpinned code at runtime (unpinned npx -y github:..., suggest-* skills overwriting local files from main, remote PROMPT.md declared trusted).

Rights: package-local licenses override root MIT for several packages (Microsoft MIT, Apache-2.0 quality-playbook and resemble-detect); four license conflicts (unattributed datasheet and MDN/tutorial copies, LGPL-like ISO data, unattributed Azure icons). GitHub Docs CC-BY material inside this GitHub-owned repository was not treated as a third-party conflict.

Accuracy: many packages carry stale or wrong version-specific claims (MCP SDK templates that do not compile, renamed PostgreSQL views, wrong React 19 statements, outdated App Store rules); these lower scores but are not hard fails.

Quality controls: 28 integration overrides recorded (19 REFERENCE-ONLY records below the 10/20 floor demoted; 7 hard fails added by a three-way second-pass adjudication of 97 REFERENCE-ONLY records whose notes mentioned ungated actions, privacy or rights; 3 static-threshold withdrawals for missing required files).

73 packages meet the computed static threshold signal (>=15/20, no hard fail, trigger/authority/dependency >=1); this marks candidates for a future governed review and is NOT verification, admission or approval.

records.dependencies: Python 3.8+, git (subprocess), local filesystem write to docs/codebase/; no network, no accounts
records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Maps an existing repository into seven evidence-cited docs under docs/codebase/ when the user explicitly asks to map/document/onboard. Not for routine feature work, bug fixes or narrow edits (stated non-trigger); it does not authorize code changes or commits.
records.content_finding: Strong evidence discipline (every claim traceable, [TODO]/[ASK USER] markers, mandatory validate-repair loop) with a safe, local, stdlib-only scanner. Minor scanner bug and no explicit treatment of untrusted README/intent docs as data; the seven-doc mandatory contract is heavy for small repos.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/scan.py (static read): stdlib only; walks cwd excluding vendor/build dirs, previews manifests (80 lines), lists entry points/lint configs, greps TODO/FIXME/HACK in source extensions, runs `git log --oneline -n 20` and `git log --since=90 days --name-only` via subprocess (no shell), counts LOC, detects CI/container/security/perf markers; writes only the --output file (mkdir parents). Bug: is_git_repo() returns True whenever git is installed (ignores returncode). Templates are fill-in skeletons with Core/Extended sections and Evidence lists; references are question lists and stack-detection tables.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Local read of repo plus git log; writes only docs/codebase/*.md and .codebase-scan.txt in the user's repo (the requested deliverable). scan.py previews .env.example/.env.template contents into the scan file (templates, not real .env), so a template that contains real values would be copied into docs. No external transmission, no consequential actions; no confirmation gate needed beyond the explicit trigger.
records.capability_specific: Evidence-backed seven-document codebase map with TODO/ASK USER markers

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 2/2: Description gives explicit trigger phrases and explicit non-triggers (feature work, bug fixes, narrow edits); focus-area mode via argument-hint.
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 2/2: Four-phase checklist, fill order for seven templates, per-template inquiry checkpoints and focus-area rules are concrete.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 2/2: Read-only analysis plus writes confined to docs/codebase/ which is the requested output; no external or destructive actions.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 1/2: Validation/repair loop and [TODO] fallback exist, but no guidance if scan.py/python/git is unavailable; is_git_repo() bug silently reports a repo.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 2/2: Output contract requires evidence lists with file paths, forbids inference, separates README intent from reality, flags devDependencies vs prod.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 2/2: Python stdlib + git only; bundled assets all present and referenced correctly (minor table formatting gap only).
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 2/2: Compatibility line honestly states Python 3.8+ and git; cross-platform paths via pathlib.
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 1/2: Useful, but codebase-mapping skills are common; differentiation is the evidence contract rather than novel mechanism.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 1/2: Warns README may be outdated but does not treat repo docs/comments as untrusted instructions; .env.example contents copied verbatim to scan output.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Code patterns for adding tool allow/deny policy, content filters, rate limits, human-approval flags, trust scores and audit trails to agent systems. Not a compliance certification or a complete security control; it does not authorize deploying or enforcing policies on live systems.
records.content_finding: Useful composable patterns with sound principles (most-restrictive-wins, fail closed, deterministic policy). Several code defects reduce effectiveness: the rate-limit counter is a global never reset per request, REVIEW just raises instead of an approval flow, decorator only wraps async functions (breaks CrewAI sync tool.func), path check uses startswith prefix, export_jsonl overwrites the 'append-only' log, and 'semantic' intent classification is plain regex.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Design guidance only; no actions performed. Example policies include send_email under require_human_approval, and fail-closed guidance. Audit trail logs error strings (could capture sensitive args) — no redaction guidance.
records.capability_specific: Policy, intent-screening, trust-scoring, and audit patterns for agent tools

rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 1/2: Patterns are explained, but integration ordering and how to wire approval is left to the reader.
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 2/2: Advisory code only; emphasizes human approval and fail-closed.

rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 1/2: Trust-score example numbers are correct, but claims like 'semantic intent classification' oversell regex matching; no evidence for thresholds/decay rate (0.001/s halves trust in ~12 min).

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Checks an agent codebase against a ten-item agentic-risk list and produces an X/10 compliance report. Should not be used as an authoritative OWASP compliance determination; it does not authorize installing the recommended toolkit.
records.content_finding: The ASI-01..ASI-10 names presented as the OWASP Agentic Security Initiative Top 10 do not match the published OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2026), whose entries are e.g. ASI01 Agent Goal Hijack, ASI02 Tool Misuse, ASI03 Identity & Privilege Abuse, ASI04 Agentic Supply Chain, ASI05 Unexpected Code Execution, ASI06 Memory & Context Poisoning, ASI07 Insecure Inter-Agent Communication, ASI08 Cascading Failures, ASI09 Human-Agent Trust Exploitation, ASI10 Rogue Agents; the skill's list (Prompt Injection, Insecure Identity, Policy Bypass, Behavioral Anomaly...) is a different taxonomy. The ASI-01 check marks PASS when any keyword like 'sanitize' appears anywhere, so 'compliance' output is misleading; the report also funnels to one vendor toolkit.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Read-only analysis; no consequential actions. Report recommends installing an unpinned PyPI package.
records.capability_specific: Map agent codebase controls to an ASI Top-10 style checklist

rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 0/2: Risk names/IDs misrepresent the OWASP list; keyword-presence = PASS; example report asserts specific controls without evidence rules.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Assembles the smallest compatible set of agent skills for a multi-step goal: derive workflow, search local index and registries, verify/rank, analyze conflicts, then stage install only after consent. Not for locating one known skill (stated); recommendation explicitly does not authorize installation, credential addition, or external publishing.
records.content_finding: One of the more safety-conscious packages: explicit consent separation, dry-run-first scripts with no-overwrite guarantees, untrusted-content threat model and hard gates. Weaknesses are Codex-centric paths, Chinese-only user-facing labels, heavy process, and a 25% adoption weight that can favor popularity over fit.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts (static): skill_index.py builds/searches a local JSON index (frontmatter, headings, SHA-256 fingerprints, Chinese/English query expansion), atomic writes only to --output; inventory_skills.py read-only inventory with regex risk indicators (destructive, credential, network, obfuscation, persistence, tokens) and Jaccard trigger overlap; project_profile.py previews/writes <project>/.codex/skill-stack.json only with --apply, refuses overwrite without --update; stage_install.py validates names, rejects symlinks, hashes files, refuses existing targets, copies via temp staging dir only with --apply and writes a lock manifest; render_stack_card.py renders HTML-escaped SVG, refuses overwrite without --force. No network calls, no subprocess, no deletes beyond its own staging temp dir. agents/openai.yaml: display metadata/default prompt.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Strong gates: 'Recommendation does not authorize installation'; staged install is dry-run by default and --apply only after approval; never overwrite existing destinations; one-click batch only with exact pins, no conflicts and explicit batch approval; no login/credentials/connector enabling without approval; safe trials must not mutate external systems; no prompt-history logging. Network discovery (npx skills, OpenCLI browser) runs third-party tooling and sends search queries externally — not separately gated.
records.capability_specific: Derive workflow, discover/rank skills, and stage audited installs with consent

records.content_finding: Exceptionally careful client and boundaries (secret handling, query-secret confirmation, atomic validated writes, structured errors, no retry loops), but its purpose is to route captures to the contributor's hosted paid service, which is vendor lock-in and third-party URL disclosure; acceptable only as reference per commercial-package rule.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/latchshot.mjs (static read): dependency-free Node CLI with capture/demo/usage commands; network calls only to fixed latchshot.fly.dev endpoints (/v1/render, /api/demo, /v1/usage); Bearer key from LATCHSHOT_API_KEY; bounded response reads (50 MB artifact, 1 MB JSON); content-type and magic-byte validation; atomic write via temp file + rename with 0600 mode, refuses overwrite without --force; no subprocess, no deletes beyond its own temp file; redacts key-like strings and URLs in errors.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Sends the target URL (and render options) to the third-party vendor; demo requests add `x-latchshot-acquisition: agentskill` attribution. Disclosed in SKILL.md; query strings require explicit `--allow-query` confirmation; credentials-in-URL, non-web ports and fragments rejected; key read only from env, never argv, never printed, error text redacted. Explicitly forbids initiating upgrade/checkout/payment. Client does not itself block localhost/private hostnames (relies on vendor side). Commercial vendor routing with account requirement.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Reference for describing breadboard layouts, 6502/65C22/28C256/555 builds and emulator behaviour. Not for authoritative electrical design or safety-critical hardware; it does not authorize programming chips or running build/flash tools.
records.content_finding: Rich and topical reference corpus, but the headline capability (HTML5 Canvas mockup rendering) is only sketched with three tiny JS object shapes, and the reference data contains several factual and cross-file inconsistencies. The verbatim vendor datasheet copy is a licensing problem for redistribution under the repo MIT license.
records.bundled_file_findings: 20 Markdown references, no scripts. Chip specs (555 datasheet transcription, 6502, 6522, 28C256, 62256, 7400, HD44780 LCD), emulator behavioural specs for each chip, breadboard build guides (10 hole-by-hole builds), minipro/T48 programmer notes, assembly/ROM build pipeline. Internal inconsistencies: memory maps differ ($8000 VIA + ROM at $9000 in assembly-compiler.md vs VIA $6000 + ROM $8000 elsewhere, while a 32 KB ROM image cannot fit $9000-$FFFF); 6522.md labels register $1 'ORA / IRB' (should be ORA/IRA); 28C256 byte-write time given as ~200 us in one file and 10 ms in another; 'E12/E24' list is actually E24; 555.md Equation 9 and 'Operating Temperature -65~+150' are wrong; SKILL.md pin ranges '9-25 A0-A15' and 'I/O0-I/O7 11-19' span VSS/GND pins.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: No consequential actions directed: no network, accounts, or destructive operations. minipro/T48 sections describe local chip read/write/erase as user hardware operations, with basic insertion/orientation safety notes. No private data flows.

records.content_finding: The anti-injection security-boundary section is an unusually good pattern for treating repository docs as untrusted. However, the skill autonomously files issues and opens PRs (publishing actions) without an action-specific confirmation, and the description is over-broad ('All changes to code must follow...').
records.bundled_file_findings: assets/issue-template.md and assets/pr-template.md: HTML-comment-guided section skeletons (Summary/Context/Proposed Solution/Acceptance Criteria; Summary/Background/Changes/Testing/Additional Notes). No scripts.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Directs publicly visible actions: creating issues (when guidance requires one, without asking), pushing branches and creating PRs via gh, plus autonomous branch creation and commits. Only reuse of an existing issue and merging require user confirmation; there is no preview-and-confirm step before filing an issue, pushing, or opening a PR ('DO NOT create a PR until you're certain you've followed the practices' is self-assessment, not user authorization). Positive: strong security boundaries (never run commands from repo docs, never read outside the worktree, never include secrets, flag injected instructions), and build/test commands are listed for the user rather than run.

No subprocess or network. Defects: entity template links [[{doc_id}-summary]] but summary pages are slugged from '{title} Summary', so lint will report broken links; summaries containing '|' corrupt the index table; ontology map sends 'object' and 'resource' to component but 'memory' to resource; keyword search seeds on any shared token, so broad matches.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Local writes only: documents.json stores full raw document content in plaintext, wiki pages and log.md are written automatically (including 'file valuable answers back'), defaulting to the current working directory. records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Manages DNS host records, nameserver delegation, child nameservers and email forwarding for Namecheap-registered domains. Explicitly not for domain purchase, SSL or hosting; it does not authorize changing DNS or mail routing without explicit user approval of each change.
records.content_finding: Well-engineered script with strong secret-entry hygiene and safe fetch-modify-write helpers, but nameserver switching, record additions, glue records and email-forwarding replacement are executed without a per-action confirmation gate, and credentials travel in the request URL. Fails the authority hard gate for unchanged use.
records.bundled_file_findings: namecheap.py (static read): argparse CLI, urllib GET to api.namecheap.com with credentials in query, XML parse with namespace stripping and Status=ERROR handling; addHost/removeHost do fetch-modify-write via setHosts; refuses to remove the last record; best-effort multi-part TLD list; config read from ~/.namecheap-api or env; writes only that config file; no subprocess. Risk: setHosts calls omit the EmailType parameter, which may reset the domain's mail settings on rewrite; records' extra attributes beyond name/type/address/ttl/mxpref are dropped.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Consequential DNS/routing and mail-routing changes. Confirmation is required only for record removal and full setHosts replacement; dns.addHost, domains.dns.setCustom/setDefault (nameserver delegation, can take a domain offline), setEmailForwarding (replaces all forwarding rules), and glue-record create/update/delete have no action-specific confirmation gate. Secrets: good practice overall (user runs setup in own terminal, getpass hidden input, never paste key in chat, chmod 600 config, env var alternative), but the API key and username are sent in the GET query string of every request (credential-bearing URL; Namecheap also accepts POST), and the config file is written before chmod (brief permission window). Public IP is obtained by calling third-party echo services, disclosing the user's IP to them.

Data flow: all documents and agent memories are sent to OpenAI for embeddings and stored in Pinecone with full original text in metadata, with no privacy/consent note. records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Decision-tree guide plus scaffold script for structuring, versioning, testing and publishing a Python library to PyPI via GitHub Actions OIDC. Not for applications/deployments or non-PyPI indexes; it does not authorize pushing tags, uploading to PyPI/TestPyPI, or changing GitHub branch/tag protection on the user's behalf.
records.content_finding: Broad, well-organized decision trees (layout, backend, versioning) and a sound OIDC publish workflow, but the agent is steered to push release tags/upload to PyPI and change branch protection with no confirmation step, which fails the authority gate. Accuracy problems are significant: the bundled scaffold produces a non-parseable pyproject.toml and an unimportable package, versioning-strategy.md names a non-existent backend `setuptools.backends.legacy:build`, claims `==0.27.*` is not valid PEP 440 (it is), pairs `license = "MIT"` with `setuptools>=68` and an MIT license classifier (PEP 639 strings need setuptools>=77, which rejects that classifier combination), and the files contradict each other on Ruff-only versus black+isort.
records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/scaffold.py (static read): stdlib only, no network/subprocess, refuses to run if the target directory exists, writes ~20 files under --output/<name>. Defects: the setuptools pyproject template contains a stray `]` after `dependencies` (generated pyproject.toml is invalid TOML); __init__.py imports `<mod>.config` which is never generated (ImportError on import); conftest passes backend= to YourClient which has no such parameter; tests/test_backends.py hard-codes `your_package`; uses `license = {text = "MIT"}` contrary to the skill's own PEP 639 rule; hatchling template ignores --layout src; computed pkg_data_key unused; .gitignore ignores all *.xml; generated CI runs black+isort while references say Ruff-only. References: nine Markdown guides with substantial duplication.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Directs consequential actions without an action-specific confirmation gate: SKILL.md and community-docs/ci-publishing/versioning-strategy give 'git tag vX.Y.Z; git push origin main --tags — this triggers publish.yml automatically' (irreversible public PyPI publication; PyPI versions cannot be re-used), manual `twine upload dist/*`, `flit publish`, and release-governance gives `gh api repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches/main/protection --method PUT` and tag-protection POST (security-control changes). The SKILL.md 'AI Agent Instruction' tells the agent to follow the decision trees, so these are agent-directed. Positive: recommends OIDC Trusted Publishing over stored tokens, 'no secrets printed in logs' checklist. No literal credentials (only placeholders like api_key="sk-..."/"test-key").
records.capability_specific: Python library packaging, versioning, CI and PyPI Trusted Publishing

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Seven-phase (plus iterations/recheck) quality-engineering audit that derives requirements, writes functional and regression tests, runs a three-pass review and a three-model spec audit, and produces BUGS.md with patches. Not a lightweight code review or a CI gate; it does not authorize applying patches to the user's source tree, mining chat/Slack/email history, sending code to third-party models, running live paid integration calls, or committing/deleting in repositories.
records.content_finding: The methodology is distinctive and evidence-minded (mechanical case-label extraction with verify.sh, executable triage probes, red/green logs, 'executed evidence outranks prose', challenge gate against false positives), which makes it strong reference material. As a package it fails: the procedure depends on a missing bin/ toolchain and schemas.md (Phase 1 must run `python -m bin.reference_docs_ingest` and stop on failure). It is internally contradictory (Phase-1-only default vs bare full run; 'no sub-agent delegation' vs agent files and challenge gate requiring sub-agents; 'STOP after each phase' vs automatic re-iteration; six vs seven exploration patterns; version stamp v1.5.3 vs v1.5.6). It also directs source-tree mutation, private-history scanning, third-party model disclosure and autonomous git/rm operations without per-action confirmation, plus a harness-override instruction.
records.bundled_file_findings: quality_gate.py (131 KB, >60 KB; characterised by imports, function index and grep): stdlib-only (json, os, re, sys, datetime, pathlib), ~78 check functions validating quality/ artifacts, sidecar JSON schemas, BUGS.md headings, TDD logs, patches, writeups, version stamps, manifests and citation invariants; all file opens are read-mode; no network, subprocess, deletes or writes; exits non-zero on FAIL. It inserts parent directories into sys.path and imports `bin.citation_verifier` if present, so running it inside an audited repo can execute that repo's bin/ code; when absent it silently downgrades byte-equality checks to WARN. SKILL.md (294 KB, read in full): phase procedures, gates and schemas. phase_prompts/*.md: runner prompt bodies with {placeholders} for the absent bin/run_playbook.py; phase4 calls `python3 -m bin.quality_playbook semantic-check` (not shipped). agents/: two orchestrator agent definitions (mandate sub-agent fan-out, web/fetch tool, harness-override clause) and an internal calibration orchestrator for the author's benchmark repos. references/: 16 Markdown protocol/templates (exploration patterns 1-7, review/spec-audit/challenge-gate protocols, verification benchmarks, run-state schema). LICENSE.txt Apache-2.0. No binaries.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Multiple consequential actions lack action-specific confirmation: (1) the TDD template in SKILL.md File 3 and RUN_TDD_TESTS protocol run `git apply quality/patches/BUG-NNN-fix.patch` directly in the working tree (and `git apply -R` with stderr suppressed), contradicting its own 'never modify outside quality/' rule; the fallback `git stash && git apply ... && git checkout . && git stash pop` can discard uncommitted work, and `git worktree remove --force` is used; recheck applies/reverses regression patches in place. (2) Step 0 'Autonomous fallback' says to scan visible chat-history folders 'without asking'; Phase 7 invites Slack/Teams/email/Jira mining. (3) Phase 4 Council of Three instructs feeding project code/requirements prompts to other vendors' models (gpt-5.4, gemini-2.5-pro) with no consent or data-handling step. (4) Integration protocol must 'exercise real external dependencies', look for API keys in .env files and run parallel live provider calls; it shows a plan but has no stop-for-approval. (5) Convergence check auto-re-iterates up to 5 full runs, and Mode B says 'Don't ask permission to add flags' for a run costing ~5-10x. (6) agents/calibration_orchestrator.md runs 'without operator intervention' with `rm -rf repos/archive/<bench>/quality/*`, `git commit`, `git revert`, nohup background processes and PID kills, and writes to the author's personal paths (~/Documents/AI-Driven Development/..., ~/Documents/QPB/...). (7) Agent files declare a 'File-writing override' that 'overrides any base harness rules' and authorizes writing AGENTS.md at the repo root. No literal credentials or telemetry found.
records.capability_specific: Multi-phase requirements-traced codebase audit with regression tests and TDD patches

rubric_dimension_rationale.trigger_precision: 1/2: explicit trigger phrases ('quality playbook', 'spec audit', 'Council of Three'), but claims to apply to 'any codebase' with no scale/cost non-triggers, and three agent entry points compete with SKILL.md.
rubric_dimension_rationale.procedural_clarity: 1/2: exhaustive gates and templates, but 294 KB with contradictory controls (default mode, sub-agent use, source-mutation boundary, stop vs auto-iterate, AGENTS.md ownership).
rubric_dimension_rationale.authority_safety: 0/2: hard gate fails, since in-tree `git apply` of fix patches, `git checkout .` fallback, autonomous chat-history scanning, third-party model disclosure, live paid API runs, and the calibration agent's rm -rf/commit/kill all proceed without explicit per-action approval.
rubric_dimension_rationale.failure_handling: 2/2: run_state.jsonl resume semantics, recoverable error events, partial-session detection, NOT_RUN/ERROR log states and explicit abort conditions.
rubric_dimension_rationale.evidence_discipline: 2/2: mechanical extraction artifacts re-verified by verify.sh, assertions with exact line citations for both confirmations and rejections, TDD red/green receipts, contradiction gate.
rubric_dimension_rationale.dependency_coherence: 0/2: essential bin/ modules (run_playbook, reference_docs_ingest, citation_verifier, run_state_lib, role_map, quality_playbook) and schemas.md/ai_context are referenced as required but not in the package; quality_gate.py silently weakens checks without them.
rubric_dimension_rationale.portability_honesty: 1/2: lists install layouts for several hosts, but embeds author-specific paths and benchmark repos, hard-codes future model IDs, and asserts unsupported statistics (35%/65%, 40-60% more bugs).
rubric_dimension_rationale.usefulness_differentiation: 2/2: requirements-derived three-pass review, enumeration two-list diff, challenge gate and executable triage probes are uncommon, transferable mechanisms.
rubric_dimension_rationale.adversarial_resilience: 1/2: strong anti-hallucination and anti-forgery controls, but no prompt-injection handling for audited repo/chat content, and quality_gate.py imports code from the target tree via sys.path.
rubric_dimension_rationale.effectiveness_design: 1/2: well-reasoned phase separation via files, but extreme size, cost multipliers and self-contradiction undermine reliable execution by an agent.

records.salvage: EXTRACT: mechanical enumeration two-list diff with saved extraction + verify.sh re-run; 'rejections must be proven by a passing assertion' triage rule; challenge-gate two-round false-positive review with scaffolding-placeholder exclusion; red/green log format with status tag first line; requirement tier/confidence tagging ([Req: formal|user-confirmed|inferred]); write-as-you-go exploration file with exact-heading gates. Rebuild with read-only default, patches validated only in a disposable worktree, explicit consent before any third-party model use or history mining, and no harness-override language.

records.content_finding: Well-built stdlib analyzer with clear exit codes, nested-set key definitions and maintenance docs. Two decisive problems: unmasked printing of potentially sensitive plan values into CI/PR output, and a gating exit code/summary that ignores non-Set attribute changes, which can make real changes look like no-ops. records.bundled_file_findings: scripts/analyze_plan.py (static, ~940 lines): stdlib argparse/json; loads references/azurerm_set_attributes.json; key-based matching of Set elements with nested definitions; primitive set comparison; markdown/json/summary output; exit codes 0-3. records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Script itself is read-only (reads plan JSON, prints to stdout). CI examples run terraform plan on pull_request and publish the analysis as a PR comment. Privacy: terraform show -json includes sensitive values in plaintext; the script only warns ('comparison may be incomplete') and still prints before/after values of modified Set-element fields via json.dumps, so secrets in Set elements (e.g., application gateway certificate password/data) can be echoed into logs and PR comments. Also --exit-code and summary/markdown outputs ignore non-Set 'other_changes', so a plan with real non-Set changes can report 'No changes detected' / exit 0 and be labelled 'Safe to ignore'.

records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Drives a GitHub PR through repeated Copilot review rounds: requests review, triages threads (fix/decline/escalate), applies fixes via sub-agents, builds/tests, commits and pushes, replies and resolves threads until convergence. records.content_finding: Engineering quality is high: deterministic convergence proof, event-id trigger verification, oscillation hard-stop, human-thread escalation default, round-cap recap gate, and carefully documented API quirks. It nonetheless fails the authority gate because pushes, PR comments and thread resolutions happen autonomously each round without an action-specific approval step, and untrusted review-comment content steers code changes.
records.bundled_file_findings: _lib.ps1: gh wrapper (temp files for stderr and quoted bodies, GraphQL error parsing, Assert-GhReady on dot-source); 01: reviewer-request mutation + copilot_work_started event verification (writes PR state); 02/03/09: read-only GraphQL snapshots, thread listing, round counting; 08: posts reply and resolves thread (writes); 10: resolves outdated Copilot threads with guards and -DryRun (writes). All network calls go only to GitHub via gh.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Autonomously performs consequential repository and communication actions with no per-action confirmation: git commit + git push every round, a 'give-up-push-commit' fallback that pushes a commit solely to re-trigger review, GraphQL requestReviewsByLogin, posting PR thread replies and resolving threads, batch-resolving outdated threads, and REVERT-AND-SHIP reverts at the recap gate ('Stay in autopilot by default'). Escalation is reserved for force-push, deletion, credentials, production, and human/advanced-security threads default to escalate-to-user; cleanup script has human-in-thread guards and -DryRun. Hardcodes a Co-authored-by: Copilot trailer regardless of actual host. No secret logging; auth delegated to gh.

records.content_finding: Methodologically strong: anti-mocking rule, fixture-contamination and tautology audits, difficulty-distribution thresholds, and a hard completion gate with a verifier script are distinctive eval design. records.purpose_and_nontrigger: Guides an agent to discover connections, construct Workflow Definition Language JSON, deploy with update_live_flow, verify, and test Power Automate flows through FlowStudio's paid MCP. Not for designing flows offline or for tenants without FlowStudio, and it does not authorize creating or changing production flows, starting them, or sending messages without explicit user approval.
records.content_finding: Technically rich and practical: it covers connectionReferences key-vs-GUID pitfalls, a dynamic-options discovery flow, the error table, and gotchas, and it puts a mandatory confirmation before test runs. It still fails the authority gate because creating, patching, starting and trigger-swapping live production flows happens with no per-action user confirmation. It is also a vendor-locked, paid-service routing skill with usage tracking.
records.bundled_file_findings: references are copy-paste WDL JSON templates (triggers, variables, control flow, Until loops, async polling, HTTP with retry/AAD OAuth, CSV parsing, SharePoint/Outlook/Teams/Approvals connector actions, build patterns). Internal inconsistencies: flow-schema.md says SharePoint Get Items 'silently caps at 256' while action-patterns-connectors.md says lists over 5,000 items are capped; action-patterns-core.md says no inline filter expression exists, yet action-patterns-data.md contrasts the action with a 'filter() expression'; the claimed default Foreach concurrency of 50 is questionable (the documented default degree of parallelism is lower). No scripts.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Directly creates and patches live tenant flows (update_live_flow), starts flows (set_live_flow_state 'Started'), swaps production triggers to a temporary HTTP trigger and back, can add flows to solutions, and lists flows in mode='admin'. None of these deployment actions has a confirmation gate. The only MANDATORY confirmation covers test runs (trigger_live_flow, resubmit_live_flow_run). Deployed recurrence/connector flows can then send emails, post Teams messages, start approvals and write to SharePoint on schedule with no further gate. Vendor telemetry: the server appends '#flowstudio-mcp' to flow descriptions for usage tracking. The Python helper models embedding the JWT as an in-code constant (placeholder '<YOUR_JWT_TOKEN>', not a literal). Patterns include SAS-signed child-flow trigger URLs (placeholder sig=<SAS>), and the guidance correctly advises securestring parameters for client secrets. IF-MATCH '*' overwrite and file-upsert patterns overwrite without conflict checks. Flow definitions and connection metadata transit the vendor server.

records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Step 8 patches the live production flow definition with update_live_flow, and Step 9 replays the failed run with resubmit_live_flow_run (it says it works for any trigger: Recurrence, SharePoint, connector webhooks), stating 'You do NOT need to ask the user to manually trigger the flow'. Replaying a run can re-send emails, re-write SharePoint items or call external HTTP endpoints. trigger_live_flow sends custom payloads to production flows. There is no confirmation step before any of these actions. Privacy: run inputs and outputs, which can contain tenant PII and secrets, go through the third-party FlowStudio service and into agent context. The skill advises slicing output and keeping secrets out of the Compose bookends. The token is shown as an inline placeholder in the source (MCP_TOKEN = "<YOUR_JWT_TOKEN>"), not read from env.

records.content_finding: Rich, practically tested API knowledge (integer --input pitfalls, project lookup by reverse issue query, preview headers). It contradicts itself: SKILL.md says MCP cannot create issues, while issue-types.md says to pass type to mcp__github__create_issue. It names the deprecated reference GitHub MCP server, and preview-only features (issue fields) are presented broadly. Writes lack pre-action confirmation and the examples target a real upstream repo.
records.bundled_file_findings: search.md: search vs list vs advanced search, qualifiers, limits. sub-issues.md: REST/GraphQL with integer --input pitfall. projects.md: Projects V2 lookup strategies, mutations, scope requirements. issue-fields.md: preview issue fields REST/GraphQL. issue-types.md: GraphQL with preview header. dependencies.md: blocked-by REST/GraphQL. milestones.md: CRUD and usage rules. images.md: Contents API image hosting, puppeteer screenshots. templates.md: bug/feature/task templates.
records.authority_and_privacy_finding: Directs many external writes (create/close issues, comments, labels/assignees, project item add/update/delete, milestone create/close/delete, sub-issue and dependency changes, branch creation and commits via Contents API for images, public gist creation) with workflow 'Execute -> Confirm: report the issue URL', meaning confirmation comes after the action rather than before. Only milestone deletion says 'only when explicitly requested'. Worked examples hard-code `repos/github/awesome-copilot/issues` as the target, which risks filing into the upstream repo. `gh auth refresh -h github.com -s project` expands credential scope without a gate. Issue bodies could disclose user content publicly. Hard gate fails.
